title: AgentCore payments: agents pay AWS Marketplace sellers on your AWS bill
caption:
Your agent can now buy things on your AWS bill.

Paid APIs usually mean a human signs up, adds a card and creates an API key. AgentCore payments now lets an agent pay x402-enabled AWS Marketplace sellers per request, in USD, with no crypto wallet.

The flow, as documented:

Discover with three read-only Gateway tools. Get a 402 quote. Call ProcessPayment with AWS_BILLING_X402. Retry with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header.

What I'd check before using it:

The payment token is valid for 5 minutes and should be treated like a credential.

Sessions are where your spend cap lives. Don't give the paying role CreatePaymentSession, or it can mint a bigger budget.

A single payment must be above $0.00 and at most $10,000.00.

At launch it supports the x402 exact scheme only.

Save this before you let an agent near a budget 🔖 What would you let yours buy first? Tell me in the comments.

Follow @shivanshu_builds for practical agent engineering on AWS.

Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/enable-ai-agents-to-pay-for-aws-marketplace-x402-products-with-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-payments/ and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/payments-process-payment.html

slides.title: The old way needs a human
paragraphs: A paid API usually means someone **signs up, adds a payment method and creates an API key**, per seller.
Now the agent pays **x402-enabled Marketplace sellers per request**, in USD, on your AWS bill. **No crypto wallet.**

slides.title: Step 3: pay the quote
slides.code:
entry = next(e for e in req["accepts"]
             if e["network"] == "aws:base")

pay = dp.process_payment(
  paymentManagerArn=ARN,
  paymentSessionId=SESSION,
  paymentInstrumentId=
    "aws.agentcorepayments.awsbilling.v1",
  paymentType="AWS_BILLING_X402",
  paymentInput={"awsBillingX402": {
    "version": "2", "payload": entry}})
